svg.text: The wide view: jitter out to high octaves
Left: the landscape stretched over 128 octaves — 38 decades of scale. At this width the jitter oscillates many times along every ribbon; the faint floor is the critical slope 1.
Right: the running mean of the local exponent against the number of octaves averaged over, for three dimensions, with its band. Few octaves: undecided. Many: separated.
128 octaves, nine dimensions

slope ↑
nothing settles; only the average does
the running mean, and its band

band = ±1 s.d. of the running mean, shrinking like 1/sqrt(octaves)
The content of the wide view: the instantaneous jitter never settles, but its RUNNING MEAN does.
So the verdict at high octaves depends only on the mean — exactly what Cascade/IntermittencyThreshold.lean formalises.
Honest limits: 128 octaves is an extrapolation of the formula, not of a flow — a real inertial range is about ten octaves, beyond which viscosity cuts the cascade off.
The roughness is synthetic; the real jitter statistics are not known to me. And in our own shell model there is no jitter at all — its per-shell bar is an exact power law.
